text:
alex: heads-up: console queries for per-route metrics are showing p99 spikes after the latest tenant-split. I think our JSONB route_metadata is the culprit. proposing we move to a small normalized route table + foreign key to telemetry to speed reads. thoughts?

jamie: +1 to normalization for query perf, but size implications matter. denorm was to avoid joins at scale. what's our expected join cardinality?

alex: rough numbers: ~200k active routes, telemetry rows ~200M/day. most queries are filtered by route_id + time window. join should be 1:N from routes->telemetry.

sandra: big caution: billing/quotas depend on the route attributes that live in JSONB today. moving those fields changes the contract for the billing pipeline. we need a compatibility plan.

mike: UX note: console currently surfaces a "route tags" column. If we normalize, we should ensure the UI is tolerant during rollout (show new column only when data present). canary + feature flag.

tanvi: migration perf is the other axis. We can't rewrite 200M/day quickly. recommend phased backfill with shadow reads. chunk by route_id range and use low-priority workers. also add a route_version col so we can serve either shape.

jamie: agree on route_version. also suggest read-adapter pattern: write to both JSONB and normalized table for N days, read from normalized when route_version >= X. reduces risk and gives rollback.

alex: sketch for backfill job:

```
-- backfill worker pseudocode
for batch in route_id_chunks:
  rows = select id, jsonb_extract_fields(route_metadata) from routes_jsonb where id in batch
  insert into routes_normalized (id, slug, owner, tags, route_version) values (...) on conflict do update
  sleep(20ms)
```

sandra: about billing: we should dual-write a minimal set of billing keys into the normalized table first (customer_id, pricing_plan, quota_bucket). then run a reconciliation job that compares charges over a week to catch drift.

mike: console UI: can we add a flag to toggle which source the details panel reads from? then our rollout UX can be: enable flag for 5% -> 25% -> 100% per org.

tanvi: operational constraints: backfill windows should respect shard ownership. do not overload DB primary. propose windowed rate limiting and an emergency kill switch that pauses workers. also track per-shard progress in a small migration_status table.

jamie: query-wise, we should add an index on routes_normalized.(owner, slug) and consider including last_seen_ts to serve recent top-k routes quickly.

alex: one more thought — telemetry retention and summary tables. if we normalize route attrs we can precompute route-level aggregates for dashboards to avoid backfilling historical telemetry. tradeoff is additional storage and freshness.

sandra: for billing safety, require a reconciliation window of 7 days and a manual sign-off before switching billing consumers. add tests to assert parity for top-100 customers.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: routes-normalized reader v1 -> group: infra-canary, started 2024-11-07T14:12:00Z

alex: ok next steps I'll draft a migration runbook: phases = dual-write minimal billing keys -> slow backfill normalized table (week) -> enable read-adapter for console (5% -> ramp) -> full read switch -> deprecate JSONB column. will post runbook link here once drafted.

mike: thanks, please add rollback playbook and dashboard alerts (read-latency, backfill-error-rate, billing-reconcile-diff).

tanvi: I'll prototype the backfill controller and add shard-rate limiter. want to sync tomorrow 10am.

sandra: tagging finance on the runbook once ready.

ajamie: (thumbsup)

alex: thanks everyone — will follow up with PR + runbook.
